x: At this point Trevor Hart discarded his warming-up shoes(!), finding them unhelpful. Although not a Tulloh he has the same habit of running bare-foot. Over the last lap Alan moved slightly ahead; with Mike in 114th position.
He was forced to give way to Card of Thames Valley and we finished the leg in 3rd place, 1 min and 44 secs behind Portsmouth(Tulloh) and 15 secs behind TVH.
Jack Brown was 21st, Charlie Dabbs (without shoes, à la Tulloh) 32nd, Masters 47th, Dooley 57th, Gebbett(recovering from gastric trouble) 60th and Johnston 64th.
Tulloh (Ports) 20:50

It was quite a tonic to see him loping along uphill and down dale to record 28:35 which was a new Club record and a time beaten only by Internationals of such class as Kilby(Coventry) Bullivant (Derby) Craig (Blackpool) Freary (Bolton) and Tulloh (Portsmouth).

Well the strongest club in the South decided to enter for the first time - yes, Portsmouth A.C, and they must be given full credit for their win, for they succeeded without the inseparable Hyman/Tulloh partnership, who were performing great feats in Belgrade.
We have all thrilled to the films of Messrs. Tulloh, Brightwell and Kilby winning gold medals. Now read the unpublicised story of the exploits of four Belgravians in Belgrade!!
Walker was fighting it out with Hyman, Tulloh and Wilkinson across a stretch of plough, when the sole of his spiked shoe tore away from its upper.
The Portsmouth team pointed out that they were without Tulloh and Johnston but would they have made over three minutes difference--I doubt it!!!
A mammoth total of 370 runners started, including 48 internationals. Tulloh was 4th, Turner 5th, Fowler 7th, Hyman 9th, Bullivant 12th, J.

He now had the invidious task of chasing Tulloh (Portsmouth) and Bullivant (Derby) who soon showed that they were in great form and we were obliged to watch our runner slowly losing the ground that Gerry North had so valiantly made up on stage VIII.
Tony Fairclough, not at his best, watched Tulloh disappear into the distance and Kerr lost further ground to Salvat, so Gerry North was faced with a deficit of 69 seconds on the final leg.

In the absence of his brother Gerry,unable to run because of a bad cold, Geoff North ran an excellent race to lead the Belgrave team and finish a very good 12th.(In front of Cooke,Hyman and Tulloh!!).

Trevor Hart hands over to Charlie Walker with Weatherill (Portsmouth) waiting to take over from the fast-finishing Tulloh. Hugh Barrow will certainly not forget his first road relay in Belgrave colours.
North (9) in the muddy thick-of-it during the Fire Brigade '2' at White City on Sept. 18th. The six runners that surround them are Gibson, Tulloh, Jackson, Stewart, Johnston, and J.

On the track John Thresher put up our best performance in sharpening up for next weeks AAA Champs., clocking a useful 1:54.7 half-mile in 4th place. In the 3 miles Gerry North was soundly beaten by Tulloh (Portsmouth) who looked as if he was running very easily for 13:32.0 .

Thresher passed Roberts down the finishing straight, only for Tulloh to pass them both and break the tape. With Bob Holt of Hercules also closing fast, only 11 seconds separated the first four at the finish.
With Johnstone and Tulloh to lead them and Hyman marshalling the remainder Pompey could well be the biggest threat unless.............. unless the holders North Staffs and Stone think otherwise.

Perhaps it was the 3 miles where those ace finishers Tulloh, Ibbottsor and Salvat all hit the final 300 yards mark together and when "Ibbo" unleashed his final effort Frankie Salvat stayed with him for 80 yards before letting loose probably the fastest 220 seen before or since in this event.

In typical Cerutty style 'Perce' claims he will do the trans-U.S.A. run (à la Tulloh) when he is 80!! Incidentally, Barry wrote his letter '..all gowned up in the labour ward of the Maternity Hospital, waiting for Myra to do her stuff again'.

Bill's best London to Brighton run was in the National event of April 1962 when he recorded 6th fastest time on the long stage 9 with only Kilby, Bullivant, Craig, Freary and Tulloh (all internationals) being faster.
